correctness.rationale: Repaired RESULT.md, scientific review, verification notes and verifier give unoriented counts 12,54,108,246 at lengths 6,8,10,12 and 130 geometric triples, profiles (6,6,6):16, (6,6,8):72, (6,8,8):36, (8,8,8):6. Canonicalization fixes the initial least vertex and chooses the smaller second vertex. The graph has no cycles of length below six; 24 vertices imply each member of any such triple has length at most 12. The witness is read with its original orientation-labelled indices; reversing factors changes at most an overall sign. An–Drummond-Cole–Knudsen Thm 4.5/Prop 4.9 identify the reduced complex with integral continuous unordered configuration homology on this graph without isolated vertices. The disjoint-inclusion product of the one-particle reduced cycle chains gives the geometric product. Independent reconstruction found 16,192 top columns, 39,600 nonzero rows, rank 16,132 over F3. All 60 witness chains are integral cycles; the 5034-term chain has nonzero distinct support, and the selected 60-coordinate minor has determinant -1. Rational nullity <=60 and the minor together make these chains a full integral basis (coordinates on the selected rows recover unique integral coefficients). Solving the transposed minor for the last basis coefficient then gave zero for all 130 geometric tori, proving the first 59 generate the product subgroup integrally and the quotient is Z. The corrected verifier was run successfully against the unchanged witness with `python3 /workspace/repairs/1/verify_nauru.py /workspace/source/2026/11/22/one-non-product-top-*/NAURU_WITNESS.json`; independent bounded replay: `python3 /tmp/opencode/check_nauru_independent.py` and the same with argument 16192. No lower-degree inference.

value.rationale: The surviving result is an exact integral geometric-generation test in a canonical 24-vertex cubic symmetric graph. Researchers comparing the obstruction across canonical graphs need to know that the quotient is primitive Z, not merely has rational rank one (which is compatible with torsion), and have an explicit lattice basis to test generators. The case does not assert first occurrence or a theorem for all such graphs. The orientation count correction changes finite supporting counts but preserves the independently verified structural invariant.
